newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firm on overseas dollar weakness.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firm on overseas dollar weakness.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee opened slightly higher against the dollar on Thursday as the market factored in an overseas weakening of the U.S. unit, but remained untraded due to a lack of sellers.
The rupee was quoted at its opening level of 57.05 at 0415 GMT. The currency closed at 57.10 on Wednesday.
"There is a lack of sellers because most banks do not have positions to sell," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by 2.75 local cents, and fixed buying and selling prices at 55.9477 and 57.0776.

Wednesday's budget, which offered incentives to exporters including the facility to borrow overseas, could signal a slower depreciation of the rupee against the dollar, said dealers at Standard Chartered Bank.
Overnight call money was at 13.5 percent, with the market well offered, dealers said.
